Kohakutou - Japanese Crystal Candy 🍬  If you’ve seen people buying the Silky Gem brand of these candies…I need you to know how cheap it is to just make them yourself at home. Recipe below! Ingredients: ½ cup water  1 tsp agar agar powder (3g) 1 cup sugar (215g) Flavor (e.g. lychee in this video)  Food coloring 1. Dissolve agar agar powder in water and bring to a simmer and stirring til dissolved.  2. Add in sugar, stir until dissolved and then mix in your desired flavouring. Simmer (small bubbles) for about 5 minutes until it thickens into a syrupy texture. Be careful not to over boil (it will spill over and make a mess). 3. Pour into a square or rectangular heat resistant container (or into candy molds) and let cool for 5-10 minutes. *Tip: if there is microfoam on top, simply use a spoon to skim it off 4. Add food coloring into whatever design or color scheme you like. 5. Cool in fridge for 2-3 hours until completely set, then remove from the container and use a knife to cut into whatever shapes you like. Tip: pile up any cuttings to form unique clusters. 6. Place on parchment paper and let dry on the counter for 4-7 days. As it dries the moisture leaves the surface and causes the sugars to crystallize, forming a crispy exterior while keeping a jelly like consistency inside! Store in airtight jars. Did you know this secret about @L’Oréal Paris’s new cushion foundation? 🫣 Well, it’s actually not really a secret since it’s right there on the ingredient list, but I was still shocked to see it! The formula contains D5 (Cyclopentasiloxane), an ingredient you won’t find in many newer complexion products anymore. A lot of brands have been reformulating to actually remove it because of stricter EU regulations. Think Dior Forever, Armani Luminous Silk, Estée Lauder Double Wear, among others. So my theory is that L’Oréal may not be planning to launch this exact formula outside of the US since reformulating for Europe would likely be necessary.
